proof_checks: Smooth exponential approximants are bounded above by the envelope plus C/beta. A fixed smooth strict approximant supplies the lower bound; beta tends to infinity before that approximant changes, so no uniform determinant lower bound is assumed. Uniform convergence gives contact support.

Continuous obstacle stability, infimum-convolution approximation from below, and bounded domination identify the lower-semicontinuous envelope. Quasi-continuous obstacles use decreasing lower-semicontinuous approximants and weighted capacity convergence. Semipositive backgrounds use one fixed Hermitian background for the product expansion.

For unbounded obstacles the envelope remains genuine under upper capping and lower truncation. The two cutoffs keep both the obstacle gap and a finite potential level; weighted bounded-product limits precede exhaustion. Continuity from below applies even when total extended mass is infinite.
Rooftop measure control partitions the common contact set without double counting and discards pluripolar poles. The fixed-point mass estimate uses its self-rooftop and contact with zero.

A strict big potential and a bounded difference envelope transfer positive Hermitian mass to each bounded potential. This is individual positivity, without a uniform positive lower mass. Semipositive bounded domination needs only that property; its stretched contact set bounds the supremum below, contradicting normalized L1 compactness if a strict gap remains.

The lower and upper volumes use all potentials in one ordinary singularity type. Bounded-change invariance, smooth-gauge invariance and scaling follow from bijections of competitors and the scaling of their currents; v-minus is the bounded-type lower volume only in the specified semipositive setting.

The relative class uses convex inequalities that remain meaningful at common poles. Convexity, bounded-change and upward stability use explicit competitors. Nested stretches stay in the class; the finite rooftop proof uses one average of N-fold stretches. The countable-family example prevents inferring sequence compactness.

Equality of ordinary envelopes for smooth obstacles follows from convex combinations and normalized L1 compactness as the reference coefficient tends to one. It does not assert bounded equivalence of the original potentials or finite mass.

In the semipositive big specialization, the difference envelope lies in the zero-reference class. A smaller-background competitor leaves a big complementary background carrying positive bounded mass. Scaling gives the uniform v-minus bound; choosing one positive delta gives individual positivity even if that bound vanishes.

The infinite-mass series has a smooth head and a genuine tail with curvature bound 2^-N. Multiplying a sufficiently late tail supplies every finite stretch. Ordinary envelope equality and trivial multiplier ideals do not control the mass of representatives; the concluding equivalence uses the existing all-potential finiteness theorem under BMP.

findings: Declare X and dimension before the opening discussion; carry settings within regimes and make changes from semipositive big to arbitrary big backgrounds explicit.
Track reference type, capacity convergence, Holder inputs, scalar uniqueness and potential selection throughout all recursive inputs.

The root retains the semipositive model-reference condition in prescribed-type existence and the relative L-infinity estimate. Its convex pair construction uses common finite truncations, and the potentially nonuniform bounded-equivalence constant supplies only a genuine envelope.
The supersolution rooftop uses contact support of the model reference to eliminate its contribution; the prescribed-type existence proof is a separate nested input still to be read.

The positive-exponent closure theorem uses capacity convergence, an exponentially decaying tail, and L1 density convergence against a finite non-pluripolar measure. At exponent zero the uniform tail bound fails, so density convergence alone does not identify the potential measure.

The singular-domination opening calls the complementary background positive, although the proof uses a semipositive big form; clarify this regime on revision. Finite truncation sets justify all subtractions when total masses are infinite.

The bounded subsolution uses a convex transform of a strict singular potential and compensating polynomial density weight. Exponential solutions decrease with the approximating backgrounds. The normalized equation instead combines upper tail envelopes and lower finite rooftops, with an exponential weight identifying the common limit. Scalar uniqueness is retained separately from potential uniqueness.
